constructions.label: Before us; come before him
constructions.analysis: Ætforan takes the dative in both supplied expressions. Ūs is first-person plural dative; him is masculine singular dative referring to the chief. The verb cuman does not change this preposition’s case here.
constructions.evidence_application: Applies the expressly datival ætforan entry to previously taught ūs and him. These exercise phrases are editorial teaching support, not dictionary quotations. The original accusative hine in the draft is corrected.

helps.analysis: Before us. Ūs is dative plural after ætforan.
Come before him. Him is dative singular, referring to the chief. Ætforan retains dative government here even with cuman; copy the whole supplied phrase.

constructions.label: Lēof as respectful address
constructions.analysis: Sir. Lēof is a substantival use of the strong masculine nominative singular adjective in direct address. This respectful address sense is supplied here; the previously taught meaning dear alone does not establish it.
constructions.evidence_application: Cook’s glossary explicitly gives sir: lēof; Crawford191 Genesis43.20 uses leof in the same address. The selected length follows Cook; no source spelling is silently normalized in the retained transcription.

constructions.label: A while ago
constructions.analysis: A while ago; formerly. Use hwīlum ǣr as a complete earlier-time expression. Hwīlum here is part of this supplied expression, rather than the frequency meaning sometimes previously learned.
constructions.evidence_application: Crawford191 Genesis43.20 has Hwilum ær we wæron her; BT576 supplies the marked headword and the same earlier-time context. The course’s selected marked spelling is retained as declared teaching composition.

constructions.label: Fill the sacks with wheat
constructions.analysis: Fill their sacks with wheat. Gefyl is a singular command; hiera saccas is the accusative plural container, and mid hwǣte names the material with dative singular hwǣte. This full material-complement frame is supplied here.
constructions.evidence_application: BT Supplement330 supports this frame for the actual lexeme ge-fyllan. Crawford19344.1 corroborates the scene with unprefixed Fille; it is not presented as exact attestation of selected Gefyl.

constructions.label: In the morning
constructions.analysis: In the morning. Morgen is accusative singular in this fixed temporal expression. Keep the whole phrase available; it does not introduce a general rule for every time expression with on.
constructions.evidence_application: BT697 directly attests On morgen. Crawford19344.3 has On mergen with morgen recorded in the apparatus. The selected form uses the existing course accusative morgen without changing its earlier analysis.

key_replacements.after: the chief remains singular **him**, dative after **ætforan** even with **cuman**.

key_support_notes.EX-XII-XIII-44-02: The learner is given **ætforan ūs** and **cuman ætforan him**, both with dative complements. The preposition determines the case; movement alone does not license **hine** here.
key_support_notes.EX-XII-XIII-45-07: **Lēof** means “sir” in this supplied respectful address, and **hwīlum ǣr** means “a while ago.” These bounded uses are given beside the task; they are not tests of the earlier senses “dear” and “sometimes.” A grammatical alternative preserving respectful address and earlier time may also satisfy Cook’s prompt.
key_support_notes.EX-XII-XIII-46-07: The visible frame **Gefyl hiera saccas mid hwǣte** supplies the material construction: **saccas** is accusative plural and **hwǣte** dative singular after **mid**. Do not grade recall of this previously untaught lexical frame.
key_support_notes.EX-XII-XIII-46-09: The fixed phrase **On morgen** is supplied with accusative singular **morgen**. Its temporal case is part of the visible help, not an inference from the earlier numbered-day construction.
